newsitem.title: USA: AST Research cutting workforce by 25 percent after loss.
newsitem.headline: AST Research cutting workforce by 25 percent after loss.

text.p: AST Research Inc. said Monday that it was cutting its workforce by 25 percent worldwide and taking a $12 million charge after suffering another big loss on sharply lower revenues.

The manufacturer of personal computers and laptops said it posted a net loss of $110 million, or $1.90 a share, for the three months ended March 29, which followed a loss of $115.8 million, or $2.59 a share, a year ago.

The company, which is being acquired by Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd, said its revenues for the quarter fell to $347 million from $530 million due to lower demand for its products and a stiff competitive pricing environment.
As a result, AST, which is based in Irvine, Calif., said it was slashing a quarter of its 4,100 employees and taking a $12 million charge in the current quarter.

"Our turnaround efforts require more aggressive actions than in the past due to lower than anticipated performance during the first quarter of fiscal year 1997," President and Chief Executive Y.S. Kim said in a statement.

"Reducing our global workforce will allow the company to significantly lower operating costs, which, combined with our continuing product development and demand generation efforts, will help to further advance our goal to return to profitability."

AST also said its first-quarter performance was affected by what it called "customer uncertainty" concerning Samsung's intention to acquire all of the outstanding shares of AST not currently owned by Samsung or its affiliates.
AST and Samsung announced April 15 that they had reached a definitive merger agreement under which Samsung would make a cash tender offer to acquire all of AST's outstanding shares for $5.40 a share.
The tender offer began Monday and will expire May 19 unless extended.
AST's stock slipped by 3.125 cents to $5.125 in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
